newsitem.title: USA: AMR sells data management services unit.
newsitem.headline: AMR sells data management services unit.

text.p: AMR Corp said Monday it sold Data Management Services, its offshore data capture and processing unit, to National Processing Co of Louisville, Ky., for an undisclosed price.

Data Management Services, with branches in Fort Worth, Barbados and the Dominican Republic, specializes in data capture and document management for companies in the insurance, financial services and transportation industries, including AMR Corp's American Airlines unit.

National Processing Co is the operating company of National Processing Inc, a publicly-traded company with sales of $373 million in 1996. National City Corp is the majority owner of National Processing Inc.
AMR said its decision to sell its Data Management Services unit was driven in part by an increase in "ticketless travel," or electronic ticketing.
"With ticketless travel becoming more and more prevalent, we have less need for data entry activity," an AMR spokesman said.
The unit, which has been part of AMR Corp since 1983, has more than 2,200 employees, or about 1.8 percent of AMR's total workforce.

Data Management becomes part of National Processing's Imaging Services Group, one of the largest U.S. third-party providers of transaction-processing services. The company processes card and check transations for merchants and other businesses.

Tom Laughlin, vice president and general manager of Data Management Services, said, "We feel the new ownership will provide additional experience and expertise for our clients and expand the scope of services DMS will be able to provide going forward. Our organization remains committed to the mutual success of our current clients as well as our new owners."
National Processing will assume the services currently provided by Data Management to American Airlines, AMR said.
